_about: Single source of truth for provider and model limits. Nothing here should be duplicated at a
call site: read it through core/provider.limits.js instead. Adding a model is one entry;
a vendor changing a number is a one-line edit that every caller picks up.
null means 'not established yet', never 'unlimited'. The accessor never invents a value, so a
null reaches the caller as null and the caller decides what to do about it.

groq: Every response carries x-ratelimit-* headers. Mind the windows, they differ:
x-ratelimit-limit-requests resets on a daily window (~24h), so it is requestsPerDay.
x-ratelimit-limit-tokens resets in well under a second, so it is tokensPerMinute.
Groq does publish a per-minute request cap but does not return it in a header; left null.
gemini: No rate-limit headers at all. The numbers come out of a 429 body:
error.details[].violations[].quotaId names the window, .quotaValue is the number.

_maxRequestTokens: A single request is billed against the per-minute token budget, so one request can never
exceed tokensPerMinute however long you wait. Confirmed by 413s at 8529 tokens on
This is the number that decides whether a whole transcript can be prompted at all.
